findings.summary: The contract lists PUT on /api/bundles/<id>/ as carrying the new fields, but only POST, GET and PATCH are tested.
findings.failure_scenario: Say the serializer marks filter_unread/filter_shared read-only for full updates, or a custom update() drops them on PUT. Then PUT {name, filter_unread: 'yes', ...} would silently keep 'off', and every test here would still pass.

findings.summary: The combination test covers search, all_tags and excluded_tags, but never any_tags.
findings.failure_scenario: Suppose a refactor of _filter_bundle applies the unread/shared filters inside the any_tags branch, or replaces the any_tags Exists condition when a state filter is set. A bundle with any_tags plus filter_unread='yes' would then return the wrong set, and no test would notice.

findings.summary: Nothing checks that values outside "off"/"yes"/"no" are rejected, though the contract says each field is one of those strings.
findings.failure_scenario: Say the model loses its choices, or the serializer field becomes a plain CharField. POST {filter_unread: 'maybe'} would then be stored and returned as 'maybe', and the bundle would quietly act as 'off'. Every test still passes.

findings.summary: On the HTML /bookmarks?bundle= page, only the yes/yes and no/no bundles are checked. 'off' and mixed combinations are only checked through the API.
findings.failure_scenario: Suppose the index view handled the bundle filter with its own code path that treats 'off' wrongly, for example as filter(unread=False). The unread_any_sharing bundle would be wrong on the page but right in the API, and nothing would catch it.

findings.summary: assertVisibleBookmarks uses count_bookmarks(), which counts once and does not retry. It is only safe because a waiting assertion on the preview count always runs first, in the same turbo-frame swap.
findings.failure_scenario: If someone calls assertVisibleBookmarks right after select_option without assertPreviewCount first, the count is read before the debounced preview reloads. It sees the stale list of 7, so the test flakes or passes against the old content.

findings.summary: The test gets the bundle id from the ORM (BookmarkBundle.objects.get) instead of the UI, so it never checks that saving leads the user to a place where the bundle can be opened.
findings.failure_scenario: Say saving the new bundle stores it but the bundles index or sidebar link to it is broken. The test still opens /bookmarks?bundle=<id> straight from the database lookup and passes. This is outside the ticket's main criteria, so the impact is small.
